milestones.title: Sections 2–3 — Quartic switch validity on the full half interval
milestones.milestone_description: For every real $0\le t\le1/2$, the exact quartic satisfies $P(t)\le\gamma_{232}(t)$ and $0<P'(t)<9$. Its tangent at $u=0.17200068185091493$ lies below $P(t)$ throughout the same interval. Both endpoints are included; the conclusion concerns the whole continuum.

milestones.title: Section 3 — A uniform entropy bound for the quartic switch
milestones.milestone_description: For every $0\le t\le1/2$, including the entropy endpoints, $H(t)<0.27905030(1+P(t))$. The coefficient is exact and the statement covers the full interval, not a finite set of samples.

milestones.title: Section 5.1 — Exact parameters and all twelve cost caps
milestones.milestone_description: The expansion-232 entropy and multiplicity constants satisfy $4.648781151243719<E_{232}<4.648781151243720$ and $0.001557987216578<\kappa_{232}<0.001557987216579$, while $H(\theta)<0.244168414687344$. The initial threshold is below $P(\theta)$, the terminal threshold is below $P(1/2)$, and $0<e(E_{232}+b)<1$. Every one of the twelve exact real costs is strictly below $1.96061388<1.960614$. These inequalities assert an analytic certificate and do not themselves assert a machine runtime.

milestones.title: Section 4.2–4.3 — Least integer quartic switch and uniform rounding bounds
milestones.milestone_description: For arbitrary positive natural block count $J$, positive even microblock size $s$, and level $0\le j<J$ with $j/J\le13/20$, let $r=(J-j)s$ and $\mu=Js$. There exists a positive least integer $q\le r/2$ satisfying the cleared integer comparison, and every smaller natural number fails it. This same $q$ satisfies $K\le P(q/r)<K+9/r$ for $K=(v+j/J)/(1-j/J)$. It also satisfies $S\le2b-j/J+(1-j/J)\gamma_{232}(q/r)$ and $(1-j/J)H(q/r)<\rho(1+v)+9\rho/\mu$. No divisibility of $J$ is needed for these per-level bounds; positivity and evenness make $r/2$ an integer and every real denominator nonzero.

milestones.title: Section 6 — Local-cover incidence and degree bounds for general expansion
milestones.milestone_description: For natural $c\ge3$ and $h>0$, set $s=2h$, $L=cs$, $M=\binom Ls$, $V=\binom Lh$, $\Delta=\binom{L-h}h$, and $G=\binom sh$. Then $V\Delta=MG$, $\Delta\le V$, $G<2^s<M$, and $\Delta^2<M2^s$. This finite statement permits expansion 232; it does not by itself establish the global encoding or machine cost.

milestones.title: Section 7 — Lower bound for the relaxed fixed-expansion cost model
milestones.milestone_description: For every real tuple $(e,b,S,\theta,\tau,\rho,R)$ satisfying the explicitly defined relaxed twelve-cost model at $c=232$, its common cost upper bound satisfies $R>1.96061349120$. The model requires $0<e<1$, $b<0$, $S>0$, $0\le\theta\le1/2$, $0\le\tau<1$, $\rho>0$, $S-2b\le\gamma_{232}(\theta)$, the whole-interval bound $H(t)\le\rho(1+\gamma_{232}(t))$, and each ledger charge at most $R$. The quantification covers all such parameter choices. This is only a lower bound for that fixed model, not for 3SUM algorithms or other expansions.

milestones.title: Sections 0, 4–6: outstanding algorithmic extension — Complete expansion-232 program and runtime bridge
milestones.milestone_description: For every positive rational $r$ strictly above all twelve costs of the fixed expansion-232 quartic parameter choice, deterministic integer 3SUM satisfies the campaign's exact shared word-RAM specification in $O(n^r)$ time. The theorem must construct a finite program for each fixed integer-size exponent, preserve distinct input positions and repetitions, reject sizes below three, and establish correctness for every sufficiently large word width together with instruction, addressing and memory costs. No solver oracle or assumed program-correctness contract is a hypothesis. This is the remaining algorithmic extension sought by this mission: the source package explicitly leaves it unproved.
